title: Check yourself: Environments, permission policies, budgets and self-hosting

questions.stem: A team creates an environment with `packages` and `limited` networking and lists the registries in `allowed_hosts`, but sets nothing else. What happens?

options.text: The packages install, since the hosts are on the allowed list
options.says: Ruled out because the page requires "also set `networking.allow_package_managers` to `true`", and listing hosts alone does not open the registries.

options.text: The request is rejected until the registry flag is true
options.says: The page says "If the environment uses `limited` networking, also set `networking.allow_package_managers` to `true`; otherwise the request is rejected with a 400 error."

options.text: The environment is created with unrestricted networking instead
options.says: Ruled out because only "a create request that omits it gets `unrestricted`", and here the field is set to `limited`.

options.text: The packages install after a warning that the agent can ignore
options.says: Ruled out because the page names a rejection and not a warning: "otherwise the request is rejected with a 400 error."

origin.section: The cloud environment: packages and the network

questions.stem: A cloud agent reads untrusted pages, keeps the default toolset policy and has `limited` networking with a few allowed hosts. Which change limits what a prompt injection can send out through those hosts?

options.text: Replace the allowed hosts with wildcard patterns
options.says: Ruled out because "The sandbox can send any request to an allowed host", so wider host patterns open more places to send to.

options.text: Switch the toolset to custom tools so that no policy applies
options.says: Ruled out because "Custom tools are executed by your application and controlled by you", so they would move the risk into your code and not remove it.

options.text: Restrict the web tools with an allowed domains list
options.says: Ruled out because the `web_search` and `web_fetch` tools "run on Anthropic's servers, so `networking` does not govern them", and a domain list on them leaves the sandbox's own route open.

options.text: Make bash wait for approval before each command
options.says: The page advises to "set the `bash` tool's policy to `always_ask` or `auto`".

origin.section: The cloud environment: packages and the network

questions.stem: A session created with a budget of `"500"` goes idle with a list cost of 503 cents. How should the team read this?

options.text: As intended, with the running request allowed to finish
options.says: The page says "The request in flight when the cap is crossed still finishes", so a paused session can read a fraction past the cap.

options.text: As a billing error that the platform should refund
options.says: Ruled out because "it bounds new work and not the exact total", so a figure past the cap is not an error.

options.text: As a failed check that ran in the middle of a request
options.says: Ruled out because "The cap is checked between requests, so it bounds new work", and not in the middle of a request.

options.text: As a crash that ended the session for good
options.says: Ruled out because "A session at its cap does not die." Its history and sandbox are kept.
